title: Course Dashboard View
description: The course frontend module shall display a dashboard listing all courses for the authenticated student.
rationale: Students need a single entry point to see and manage all their courses without navigating to each one individually.

title: Intake Chat View
description: The course frontend module shall display a real-time chat view for courses in intake status.
rationale: Students must be able to converse with the AI Chair agent to complete the intake process before a syllabus can be drafted.

title: Syllabus Draft View
description: The course frontend module shall display the generated syllabus and allow student approval or modification requests.
rationale: Students must review and either accept or request changes to the AI-generated syllabus before course content is created.

title: Due-Date Schedule View
description: The course frontend module shall display the due-date schedule and require explicit student agreement before proceeding.
rationale: Students must acknowledge homework deadlines before content generation begins, establishing a binding commitment.

title: Generating View
description: The course frontend module shall display a progress view while course content is being generated.
rationale: Content generation takes several minutes; students need feedback that the system is working and to be automatically advanced when ready.

title: Course Hub View
description: The course frontend module shall display a hub view for active and completed courses with sections and homework.
rationale: Students need a central place to navigate course sections, track homework due dates, and manage enrollment status.

title: SSE Event Stream Connection
description: The course frontend module shall maintain an authenticated real-time event stream connection for courses.
rationale: The browser EventSource API does not support custom headers, so fetch must be used to authenticate SSE connections.

title: Status-Based View Routing
description: The course frontend module shall route each course to the view matching its current status.
rationale: Each course status corresponds to a distinct workflow step; routing ensures the student always sees the correct interaction surface.

title: Create Course Modal
description: The course frontend module shall provide a modal form for creating a new course with a single topic field.
rationale: A focused modal keeps course creation discoverable from the dashboard without navigating away from the course list.

title: Dashboard: Fetch Course List
description: The course frontend module shall load the student's course list when the dashboard is mounted.
rationale: The dashboard must be populated with live data on every visit to reflect any status changes since the last session.

title: Dashboard: Course Card Display
description: The course frontend module shall display each course card with its title or topic, status, and creation date.
rationale: Students need enough information on each card to identify a course and understand its current lifecycle stage.

title: Dashboard: Empty State
description: The course frontend module shall display an empty-state message and create button when the course list is empty.
rationale: A first-time student must be clearly guided to create their first course rather than seeing a blank page.

title: Dashboard: Create Course Button
description: The course frontend module shall display a create-course button that opens the create-course modal.
rationale: Students need a persistent, discoverable way to initiate a new course from the dashboard.

title: Dashboard: Card Navigation
description: The course frontend module shall navigate to the status-appropriate view when a course card is clicked.
rationale: Each course status maps to a distinct view; clicking a card must drop the student directly into the correct workflow step.

title: Intake View: SSE Connection
description: The course frontend module shall open a real-time event stream connection when the intake view mounts.
rationale: Pipeline events must be streamed in real time during intake so the student receives immediate agent feedback.

title: Intake View: Event Display
description: The course frontend module shall render each incoming pipeline event as a status message in the intake view.
rationale: Students must see agent progress updates as they arrive to know the intake process is active and progressing.

title: Intake View: Chat Input
description: The course frontend module shall provide a text field and send button for submitting chat messages during intake.
rationale: The intake process is conversational; students must be able to send messages to the Chair agent at any point.

title: Intake View: Conversation History
description: The course frontend module shall display alternating student and assistant messages in chronological order.
rationale: Students need to see the full conversation thread to understand context and craft appropriate follow-up messages.

title: Intake View: Status Transition Navigation
description: The course frontend module shall navigate to the syllabus draft view when a pipeline event signals status is syllabus_draft.
rationale: Automatic navigation removes friction; students should not need to manually refresh or navigate after intake completes.

title: Intake View: SSE Reconnect
description: The course frontend module shall retry the event stream connection with exponential backoff on drop, up to five attempts.
rationale: Transient network failures must not permanently break the real-time event stream; bounded retries prevent infinite loops.

title: Syllabus Draft View: Content Display
description: The course frontend module shall display the latest syllabus content in the syllabus draft view.
rationale: Students must read the full AI-generated syllabus before deciding to approve or request changes.

title: Syllabus Draft View: Approve Button
description: The course frontend module shall display an approve button that submits the syllabus approval.
rationale: Students need a single clear action to accept the syllabus and advance the course to schedule agreement.

title: Syllabus Draft View: Modification Request
description: The course frontend module shall open a text-area modal and submit the student's modification notes.
rationale: Students may need changes to the syllabus; a modal with a free-text field lets them describe what should be revised.

title: Syllabus Draft View: Fetch Syllabus
description: The course frontend module shall load the latest syllabus for the course on syllabus draft view mount.
rationale: The syllabus content must be loaded fresh on each visit so the student always sees the most recent version.

title: Schedule View: Due-Date List Display
description: The course frontend module shall display homework titles and due dates in the due-date schedule view.
rationale: Students must be able to review every deadline before committing, as due dates cannot be changed after agreement.

title: Schedule View: Irreversibility Warning
description: The course frontend module shall display a warning that due dates cannot be changed after agreement.
rationale: Students must be informed of the binding nature of schedule agreement before they commit.

title: Schedule View: Agree Button
description: The course frontend module shall submit the student's schedule agreement when the agree button is clicked.
rationale: The API must record the student's explicit agreement to the schedule before content generation can begin.

title: Generating View: Progress Message
description: The course frontend module shall display a generation-in-progress message in the generating view.
rationale: Students need clear feedback that the system is working so they do not abandon the session or reload prematurely.

title: Generating View: SSE Event Display
description: The course frontend module shall stream and display pipeline events while course content is being generated.
rationale: Pipeline events during content generation give students visibility into what the system is doing, reducing perceived wait time.

title: Generating View: Transition to Active
description: The course frontend module shall navigate to the course hub view when a pipeline event signals status is active.
rationale: Students must be automatically advanced to the course hub once generation completes, removing the need for a manual refresh.

title: Course Hub View: Course Header
description: The course frontend module shall display the course topic and status in the course hub view header.
rationale: Students need immediate confirmation of which course they are viewing and its current lifecycle status.

title: Course Hub View: Section List
description: The course frontend module shall list all syllabus sections with navigation links in the course hub view.
rationale: Students navigate course content section by section; the hub must expose all sections with direct links to each reader.

title: Course Hub View: Homework List
description: The course frontend module shall display homework assignments with due dates and submission status.
rationale: Students must be able to track upcoming and past homework assignments and their submission state from the hub.

title: Course Hub View: Withdraw and Resume Actions
description: The course frontend module shall display a withdraw button for active courses and a resume button for archived courses.
rationale: Students must be able to pause (withdraw) or re-enter (resume) a course directly from the hub without navigating elsewhere.

title: SSE Client: Fetch-Based Connection
description: The course frontend module shall open SSE connections using an authenticated streaming request.
rationale: The browser EventSource API cannot send custom headers; fetch must be used so the JWT is transmitted with the request.

title: SSE Client: Resume After Last Event
description: The course frontend module shall pass ?after={lastEventId} on SSE reconnect to resume from the last received event.
rationale: Resuming from the last event ID prevents duplicate display of events and ensures no pipeline events are missed on reconnect.

title: SSE Client: Keepalive Handling
description: The course frontend module shall silently discard SSE comment lines beginning with a colon.
rationale: The server sends keepalive comments to prevent connection timeouts; these must not be rendered as events.

title: SSE Client: Connection Cleanup
description: The course frontend module shall close the SSE connection when the consuming view is unmounted.
rationale: Leaving open connections after navigation wastes resources and may deliver stale events to an already-destroyed component.

title: Routing: Intake Status
description: The course frontend module shall route a course with status intake to the intake chat view.
rationale: The intake chat view is the only appropriate surface for a course that has not yet completed its intake conversation.

title: Routing: Syllabus Draft Status
description: The course frontend module shall route a course with status syllabus_draft to the syllabus draft view.
rationale: Once intake is complete the student must review the draft syllabus; routing ensures they land there automatically.

title: Routing: Syllabus Approved Status
description: The course frontend module shall route a course with status syllabus_approved to the due-date schedule view.
rationale: After syllabus approval the only required student action is agreeing to the schedule; direct routing removes unnecessary steps.

title: Routing: Generating Status
description: The course frontend module shall route a course with status generating to the generating view.
rationale: Content generation is a distinct waiting phase; students should see progress events rather than the hub before content exists.

title: Routing: Active Status
description: The course frontend module shall route a course with status active to the course hub view.
rationale: An active course has all its content available; the hub is the correct landing point for day-to-day student interaction.

title: Routing: Archived Status
description: The course frontend module shall route a course with status archived to the course hub view.
rationale: Archived courses remain readable; students should still see course content and have access to the resume action.

title: Routing: Completed Status
description: The course frontend module shall route a course with status completed to the course hub view.
rationale: Completed courses are read-only; the hub view correctly presents content without modification actions.

title: Create Course Modal: Topic Field
description: The course frontend module shall render a single topic text field inside the create-course modal.
rationale: Course creation requires only a topic; a minimal form reduces friction and cognitive load for new students.

title: Create Course Modal: Submit
description: The course frontend module shall submit the course creation request when the modal form is submitted.
rationale: The backend requires a JSON body with a topic field to create a course; the modal must conform to this contract.

title: Create Course Modal: Close on Success
description: The course frontend module shall close the create-course modal after successful course creation.
rationale: After successful creation the student should be immediately placed in the intake workflow without additional clicks.

title: Create Course Modal: Conflict Error
description: The course frontend module shall display an already-active-course error message on a 409 response.
rationale: Students can only have one active course; a 409 must surface a clear, human-readable message rather than a generic error.

title: Create Course Modal: Close Without Submitting
description: The course frontend module shall close the create-course modal and discard input when the student dismisses it.
rationale: Students must be able to cancel course creation without unintended side effects or stale state in the form.

title: Create Course Modal: Add Course to List on Success
description: The course frontend module shall add the newly created course to the dashboard list on success.
rationale: Immediately adding the course to the list avoids a full refetch and lets the student see their new course without delay.

title: Create Course Modal: Navigate to Intake on Success
description: The course frontend module shall navigate to the intake view for the newly created course.
rationale: Students must begin the intake conversation immediately after creating a course; automatic navigation removes a manual step.

title: Dashboard: GET /api/v1/courses Request
description: The course frontend module shall send GET /api/v1/courses with the Authorization header on dashboard mount.
rationale: The list endpoint requires a valid JWT; the request must be authenticated to return courses scoped to the student.

title: Dashboard: Loading State During Fetch
description: The course frontend module shall show a loading indicator while the course list request is in flight.
rationale: Slow networks may delay the response; a loading indicator prevents the student from thinking the page is broken.

title: Dashboard: Render Courses on 200
description: The course frontend module shall render a course card for each object in the courses array from the 200 response.
rationale: The API returns a JSON object with a courses array; the UI must iterate that array to produce one card per course.

title: Dashboard: Fetch Error Display
description: The course frontend module shall display a fetch-error message when GET /api/v1/courses returns a non-200 status.
rationale: Students must know when the course list could not be loaded so they can retry or report the issue.

title: Dashboard: Course Card Title with Topic Fallback
description: The course frontend module shall display title on each dashboard card, or topic when title is empty.
rationale: The AI pipeline sets title after course creation; before it is set the topic is the only available human-readable identifier, so cards must never show a blank heading.

title: Dashboard: Course Card Status and Date
description: The course frontend module shall display the status and created_at fields on each dashboard course card.
rationale: Status and creation date give students context about each course's stage and age at a glance.

title: Dashboard: Empty State Message
description: The course frontend module shall display "You have no courses yet." and a create button when no courses exist.
rationale: An actionable empty state guides new students instead of showing a confusing blank list.

title: Dashboard: Create Button Opens Modal
description: The course frontend module shall open the create-course modal when the create-course button is clicked.
rationale: The create button is the primary call-to-action on the dashboard; clicking it must immediately reveal the creation form.

title: Dashboard: Card Click Navigates by Status
description: The course frontend module shall navigate to the route for the course's current status when a course card is clicked.
rationale: Clicking a card must take the student directly to the appropriate workflow view without an intermediate step.

title: Intake View: Fetch SSE with Auth Header
description: The course frontend module shall open GET /api/v1/courses/{id}/events using fetch with the Authorization header.
rationale: EventSource cannot send Authorization headers; fetch with a streaming reader is required for authenticated SSE.

title: Intake View: Parse SSE Lines
description: The course frontend module shall parse incoming text/event-stream data line by line into event-type and data fields.
rationale: The SSE protocol encodes events as lines with event: and data: prefixes; correct parsing is required to extract payloads.

title: Intake View: SSE Connection on Mount
description: The course frontend module shall initiate the SSE connection immediately when the intake view is mounted.
rationale: Pipeline events may have been emitted before mount; connecting immediately allows the client to receive any queued events.

title: Intake View: Render Pipeline Event Payload
description: The course frontend module shall render each SSE event's payload as a status message in the event list.
rationale: Each pipeline event carries a payload with agent status information that the student must be able to read.

title: Intake View: Append Events in Order
description: The course frontend module shall append each new pipeline event below the previous ones in arrival order.
rationale: Events are emitted chronologically; displaying them in arrival order preserves the logical narrative of the intake process.

title: Intake View: Chat POST Request
description: The course frontend module shall send POST /api/v1/courses/{id}/chat with body {"message": string} on chat submit.
rationale: The chat endpoint requires a JSON body with a message field; the client must conform to this contract exactly.

title: Intake View: Disable Input While Awaiting Reply
description: The course frontend module shall disable the chat input and send button while a chat POST request is in flight.
rationale: Preventing concurrent submissions while awaiting the agent's reply avoids out-of-order message sequences.

title: Intake View: Typing Indicator
description: The course frontend module shall display a typing indicator while waiting for the chat POST response.
rationale: A typing indicator signals that the agent is processing the message, so students do not assume the system is unresponsive.

title: Intake View: Append Student Message Optimistically
description: The course frontend module shall append the student's message to the conversation history immediately on submit.
rationale: Optimistic display makes the conversation feel responsive; the student sees their message without waiting for the round trip.

title: Intake View: Append Assistant Reply on 200
description: The course frontend module shall append the reply field from the 200 chat response as an assistant message.
rationale: The chat endpoint returns {"reply": string}; the UI must extract and display that field as the assistant's turn.

title: Intake View: Chat Error Display
description: The course frontend module shall display an error message and re-enable input when the chat POST returns a non-200 status.
rationale: Chat failures must be surfaced so the student can retry; re-enabling the input prevents a stuck form.

title: Intake View: Student Message Alignment
description: The course frontend module shall display student messages right-aligned and assistant messages left-aligned.
rationale: Conventional chat alignment immediately distinguishes who sent each message without additional labels.

title: Intake View: Conversation Scroll
description: The course frontend module shall scroll the conversation panel to the latest message after each new message is added.
rationale: Without auto-scroll, new messages appear off-screen and the student must scroll manually after every turn.

title: Intake View: Navigate on syllabus_draft Event
description: The course frontend module shall navigate to the syllabus draft view when an SSE event carries a status of syllabus_draft.
rationale: Automatic navigation removes the need for the student to manually refresh or identify when intake has completed.

title: SSE Reconnect: Exponential Backoff Delays
description: The course frontend module shall wait 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16 seconds between successive SSE reconnect attempts.
rationale: Exponential backoff reduces server load during outages and prevents a thundering-herd reconnect storm.

title: SSE Reconnect: Maximum Five Attempts
description: The course frontend module shall stop retrying the SSE connection after five consecutive failed attempts.
rationale: Unlimited retries waste resources; five attempts are sufficient to survive transient failures without looping indefinitely.

title: SSE Reconnect: Exhaustion Error Message
description: The course frontend module shall display a connection-failure message after all five SSE reconnect attempts are exhausted.
rationale: Students must know the live event stream is unavailable so they can reload the page or seek support.

title: Syllabus Draft View: Fetch Syllabus Content
description: The course frontend module shall fetch the latest syllabus for the course and display its content_adoc field.
rationale: The AsciiDoc content stored in content_adoc is the canonical syllabus text; it must be fetched and rendered for the student.

title: Syllabus Draft View: Loading State
description: The course frontend module shall display a loading indicator while the syllabus content is being fetched.
rationale: Syllabus documents may be large; a loading indicator prevents the student from seeing an empty view during fetch.

title: Syllabus Approve: POST Request
description: The course frontend module shall send POST /api/v1/courses/{id}/syllabus/approve with the Authorization header.
rationale: The approve endpoint requires authentication to verify the student owns the course before changing its status.

title: Syllabus Approve: Disable Button During Request
description: The course frontend module shall disable the approve button while the approve POST request is in flight.
rationale: Disabling the button prevents double-submission, which would attempt an invalid state transition on the already-approved course.

title: Syllabus Approve: Navigate on 200
description: The course frontend module shall navigate to the due-date schedule view when the approve POST returns 200.
rationale: A 200 confirms the course has moved to syllabus_approved; the student must be routed to agree to the schedule next.

title: Syllabus Approve: 409 Error Display
description: The course frontend module shall display an invalid-transition error message when the approve POST returns 409.
rationale: A 409 means the course is not in syllabus_draft status; the student must be informed that the action is no longer valid.

title: Syllabus Approve: Generic Error Display
description: The course frontend module shall display a generic error message when the approve POST returns any other non-200 status.
rationale: Unexpected server errors must surface a user-facing message rather than silently failing or leaving the button disabled.

title: Modification Modal: Open on Button Click
description: The course frontend module shall open a modal with a text area when the request-modification button is clicked.
rationale: A dedicated modal keeps the modification notes separate from the syllabus view and gives the student adequate writing space.

title: Modification Modal: POST Request
description: The course frontend module shall send POST /api/v1/courses/{id}/syllabus/modification with body {"request": string}.
rationale: The modification endpoint expects a request field containing the student's notes; the body key must be request, not notes.

title: Modification Modal: Disable Submit During Request
description: The course frontend module shall disable the modal submit button while the modification POST is in flight.
rationale: Disabling the submit button prevents duplicate modification requests being sent while the first is still processing.

title: Modification Modal: 200 Success Message
description: The course frontend module shall close the modal and display a modification-submitted confirmation message on 200.
rationale: Students must know their request was accepted; the confirmation message removes ambiguity about whether the action succeeded.

title: Modification Modal: Reload Syllabus After 200
description: The course frontend module shall reload the syllabus content after a successful modification request.
rationale: The backend records a new syllabus version on modification; the view must refresh to show the updated version number.

title: Modification Modal: Error Display
description: The course frontend module shall display an error message inside the modal when the modification POST returns non-200.
rationale: Errors must be shown in context so the student can correct their input or retry without losing the modal state.

title: Syllabus Draft View: Fetch on Mount
description: The course frontend module shall initiate the syllabus fetch immediately when the syllabus draft view is mounted.
rationale: Early fetching minimises the time the student spends looking at a loading indicator before the syllabus appears.

title: Syllabus Draft View: Fetch Error Display
description: The course frontend module shall display a fetch-error message when the syllabus fetch returns a non-200 status.
rationale: If the syllabus cannot be loaded the student must be told rather than seeing an empty or frozen view.

title: Schedule View: Display Homework Titles
description: The course frontend module shall display the title of each homework item in the due-date schedule list.
rationale: Students must be able to identify each assignment by name to understand what they are committing to complete.

title: Schedule View: Display Due Dates
description: The course frontend module shall display the due_date for each homework item formatted as a human-readable date.
rationale: Raw ISO timestamps are not student-friendly; formatted dates make deadlines immediately understandable.

title: Schedule View: Irreversibility Warning Text
description: The course frontend module shall display the text "Once you agree, due dates cannot be changed." above the agree button.
rationale: Students must see a clear warning before committing to a schedule that will be binding for the duration of the course.

title: Schedule Agree: POST Request
description: The course frontend module shall send POST /api/v1/courses/{id}/schedule/agree with the Authorization header.
rationale: The schedule/agree endpoint requires authentication to confirm the student owns the course before recording agreement.

title: Schedule Agree: Disable Button During Request
description: The course frontend module shall disable the agree button while the schedule/agree POST is in flight.
rationale: Disabling the button prevents double-submission which would attempt to agree to a schedule with no remaining pending entries.

title: Schedule Agree: Navigate to Generating on 200
description: The course frontend module shall navigate to the generating view when the schedule/agree POST returns 200.
rationale: A 200 confirms all due dates are agreed; the backend will begin content generation and the student should see that view.

title: Schedule Agree: 409 Error Display
description: The course frontend module shall display a no-pending-schedule error message when schedule/agree returns 409.
rationale: A 409 means there are no unagreed due dates; the student must be informed so they can navigate away or refresh.

title: Schedule Agree: Generic Error Display
description: The course frontend module shall display a generic error message when schedule/agree returns any other non-200 status.
rationale: Unexpected server failures must not silently leave the agree button disabled; students need a message to act on.

title: Generating View: Static Progress Message
description: The course frontend module shall display a static message that course content generation may take several minutes.
rationale: Setting time expectations prevents students from assuming an error when generation takes longer than they expected.

title: Generating View: SSE Connection
description: The course frontend module shall open GET /api/v1/courses/{id}/events using fetch with the Authorization header on generating view mount.
rationale: Content generation pipeline events must stream to the student in real time, requiring an authenticated SSE connection.

title: Generating View: Render Pipeline Events
description: The course frontend module shall render each incoming SSE pipeline event as a status message in the generating view.
rationale: Showing generation progress events lets students track what the agent is doing rather than watching a static spinner.

title: Generating View: Navigate on Active Event
description: The course frontend module shall navigate to the course hub view when an SSE event carries a status of active.
rationale: Automatic navigation once generation completes removes the need for a manual refresh and delivers the student to their content immediately.

title: Course Hub: Display Topic and Status
description: The course frontend module shall display the course topic and current status in the hub view header.
rationale: The header orients the student to which course they are viewing and whether it is active, archived, or completed.

title: Course Hub: Render Section List
description: The course frontend module shall render one list item per syllabus section in the course hub view.
rationale: Students navigate course content section by section; every section must be listed so none are inaccessible.

title: Course Hub: Section Navigation Links
description: The course frontend module shall render each section list item as a navigation link to the section reader view.
rationale: Sections must be clickable; plain text items would require students to know the direct URL for each section.

title: Course Hub: Homework Assignment List
description: The course frontend module shall display each homework assignment's title and due date in the hub view.
rationale: Students track deadlines from the hub; every homework item must be listed with its due date visible without additional navigation.

title: Course Hub: Homework Submission Status
description: The course frontend module shall display the submission status for each homework assignment in the hub view.
rationale: Students need to see at a glance which assignments are submitted and which are still outstanding.

title: Course Hub: Withdraw Button Visibility
description: The course frontend module shall display the withdraw button only when the course status is active.
rationale: Withdrawal is only a valid action for active courses; showing it for other statuses would allow invalid transitions.

title: Course Hub: Withdraw POST Request
description: The course frontend module shall send POST /api/v1/courses/{id}/withdraw with the Authorization header.
rationale: The withdraw endpoint requires authentication to confirm the requesting user owns the course before archiving it.

title: Course Hub: Navigate to Dashboard After Withdraw 200
description: The course frontend module shall navigate to the dashboard when the withdraw POST returns 200.
rationale: After withdrawal the course is archived; the student should return to the dashboard to see the updated course state.

title: Course Hub: Withdraw Error Display
description: The course frontend module shall display an error message when the withdraw POST returns a non-200 status.
rationale: Withdrawal failures must be surfaced so the student knows the course was not archived and can retry.

title: Course Hub: Resume Button Visibility
description: The course frontend module shall display the resume button only when the course status is archived.
rationale: Resume is only valid for archived courses; displaying it for other statuses exposes an action that would return a 409.

title: Course Hub: Resume POST Request
description: The course frontend module shall send POST /api/v1/courses/{id}/resume with the Authorization header.
rationale: The resume endpoint requires authentication to confirm ownership and performs the archived-to-prior-status transition.

title: Course Hub: Navigate After Resume 200
description: The course frontend module shall navigate to the status-appropriate view after the resume POST returns 200.
rationale: Resume restores the pre-withdrawal status; the student must be routed to the correct view for that restored status.

title: Course Hub: Resume 409 Error Display
description: The course frontend module shall display an already-active-course error message when resume POST returns 409.
rationale: A 409 means the student already has an active course; they must be told before they can proceed with the conflict resolved.

title: SSE Client: Authorization Header
description: The course frontend module shall include the Authorization: Bearer {token} header in every SSE fetch request.
rationale: The SSE endpoint validates the JWT to enforce course ownership; omitting the header returns 401 and no events.

title: SSE Client: ReadableStream Line Reader
description: The course frontend module shall read the SSE response body as a ReadableStream and process it line by line.
rationale: SSE over fetch requires consuming the response body as a stream; buffered reads would miss events that arrive in chunks.

title: SSE Client: After Query Parameter on Reconnect
description: The course frontend module shall append ?after={lastEventId} to the SSE URL when reconnecting after receiving at least one event.
rationale: The server uses the after parameter to return only events newer than the last received, preventing duplicate display.

title: SSE Client: Discard Comment Lines
description: The course frontend module shall skip any SSE line that begins with a colon without dispatching it as an event.
rationale: The server emits ": keepalive" comments every two seconds; treating them as events would pollute the event list.

title: SSE Client: Abort on Unmount
description: The course frontend module shall call abort() on the SSE fetch AbortController when the consuming view is unmounted.
rationale: Aborting the fetch on unmount terminates the underlying TCP connection and prevents memory leaks from orphaned stream readers.

title: Create Course Modal: Single Topic Input
description: The course frontend module shall render exactly one text input labelled Topic in the create-course modal.
rationale: Course creation requires only a topic string; additional fields would add unnecessary friction to the onboarding flow.

title: Create Course Modal: Non-Empty Validation
description: The course frontend module shall prevent submission and display a validation message when the topic field is empty.
rationale: The backend rejects empty topics with a 400; client-side validation avoids an unnecessary round trip.

title: Create Course Modal: POST Body Shape
description: The course frontend module shall post {"topic": string} as the JSON body when submitting the create-course form.
rationale: The backend createCourse handler decodes a topic field from the JSON body; any other field name will result in a 400.

title: Create Course Modal: Disable Submit During POST
description: The course frontend module shall disable the submit button while the create-course POST is in flight.
rationale: Disabling the submit button prevents duplicate course creation requests that would return 409 on the second attempt.

title: Create Course Modal: Authorization Header
description: The course frontend module shall include the Authorization: Bearer {token} header in the create-course POST request.
rationale: The create endpoint reads the user ID from the JWT to associate the course with the authenticated student.

title: Create Course Modal: Content-Type Header
description: The course frontend module shall send Content-Type: application/json in the create-course POST request.
rationale: The handler uses json.NewDecoder to parse the body; without the correct content type the body may not be decoded.

title: Create Course Modal: Close on 201
description: The course frontend module shall close the create-course modal when the POST returns 201.
rationale: Once the course is created the modal has served its purpose; closing it reveals the dashboard with the new course.

title: Create Course Modal: Prepend New Course to List
description: The course frontend module shall add the 201 response course object to the top of the dashboard course list.
rationale: Prepending avoids a full list refetch and immediately shows the student their new course at the top, matching creation order.

title: Create Course Modal: Navigate to Intake on 201
description: The course frontend module shall navigate to the intake view for the new course ID from the 201 response.
rationale: The student must begin the intake conversation immediately after creating a course; automatic navigation removes a manual step.

title: Create Course Modal: 409 Error Message
description: The course frontend module shall display "You already have an active course. Complete or archive it first." on 409.
rationale: Students may not know they already have an active course; an exact, actionable message tells them what to do next.

title: Create Course Modal: Dismiss Clears Input
description: The course frontend module shall reset the topic field to empty when the create-course modal is dismissed without submitting.
rationale: Stale topic text must not persist when the modal is reopened, which would create a confusing pre-filled state.

title: Intake View: Load Chat History on Mount
description: The course frontend module shall load and display the full prior chat history when the intake view mounts.
rationale: Students returning to an in-progress intake session must see all prior messages; an empty chat on reload would force the student to repeat earlier answers.

title: Intake View: Input Bar Always Visible
description: The course frontend module shall render the chat input bar within the application layout viewport at all times.
rationale: When the chat view uses a height that exceeds the available space below the navigation bar, the input bar is pushed below the visible viewport and the student cannot type a message.

title: Intake View: Load Chat History on Mount
description: The course frontend module shall request prior chat history from the server when the intake view mounts.
rationale: The chat panel must show the prior conversation, including the agent's opening question, so the student can resume where they left off.

title: Intake View: Render History Messages
description: The course frontend module shall populate the conversation panel with messages from the history response before accepting new input.
rationale: History messages must appear before the student can send a new message so the conversation context is visible at the time of their next reply.

title: Intake View: Viewport-Relative Height
description: The course frontend module shall constrain the intake chat view height to the space remaining below the navigation bar.
rationale: Using the full viewport height (100vh) ignores the navigation bar height and pushes the input bar below the visible area, making it unreachable without scrolling the page.

title: Intake View: Course Preparation Indicator
description: The course frontend module shall indicate that course preparation is in progress while the intake conversation is empty.
rationale: The opening question is generated asynchronously after course creation; without an indicator the student sees a blank page and assumes nothing is happening.

title: Intake View: Refresh History Until Opening Message
description: The course frontend module shall refresh the chat history periodically until the first message arrives.
rationale: The opening question lands a few seconds after the view mounts; a single fetch on mount misses it and the student never sees it without a manual reload.

title: Intake View: Preparation Wait Bounded
description: The course frontend module shall stop refreshing after a bounded wait and invite the student to begin typing.
rationale: Opening-question generation can fail permanently; the student must be told they can start the conversation themselves rather than waiting forever.

title: Syllabus View: Drafting Indicator While Generating
description: The course frontend module shall indicate that syllabus drafting is in progress when no syllabus exists yet.
rationale: Syllabus generation runs in the background after intake completes; showing a failure message while the system is working misleads the student.

title: Syllabus View: Refresh Until Syllabus Available
description: The course frontend module shall refresh periodically until the syllabus becomes available or a bounded wait elapses.
rationale: The student is redirected to the syllabus view while generation is still running; without refreshing they would be stuck on a stale page.
